questions.questionText: What does variance measure about a dataset?
options: The single average value of the data
How spread out the data is around its mean
The total number of data points
Whether the data is normally distributed
questions.correctAnswer: How spread out the data is around its mean
questions.explanation: Variance is the average squared deviation from the mean — low variance means values cluster tightly, high variance means they're widely spread.

questions.questionText: What does a logistic regression model's output actually estimate, in probability terms?
options: The mean of a normal distribution
The parameter p of a Bernoulli distribution — the probability of the "yes" outcome
The variance of the input features
A completely deterministic value with no probabilistic interpretation
questions.correctAnswer: The parameter p of a Bernoulli distribution — the probability of the "yes" outcome
questions.explanation: Binary classification's probability output is exactly the p parameter of a Bernoulli distribution — the model is estimating how likely the "positive" outcome is for each input.

questions.questionText: What transformation does standardizing a feature (subtracting the mean, dividing by standard deviation) accomplish?
options: It rescales the feature so its mean becomes 0 and its standard deviation becomes 1, putting it on a comparable scale to other features
It converts the feature into a categorical variable
It has no effect on the data's distribution shape
questions.correctAnswer: It rescales the feature so its mean becomes 0 and its standard deviation becomes 1, putting it on a comparable scale to other features
questions.explanation: This is exactly what scikit-learn's StandardScaler computes, and exactly why it addresses the feature-scaling issue raised in the KNN lesson — putting features on comparable scales before distance-based computations.
